name: HVAC Schedule Drift
trigger_conditions: HVAC runtime may exceed actual occupied or service-relevant windows
anti_triggers: runtime already aligned to occupancy and service windows
HVAC systems are minor or not owner-controlled
schedule evidence shows no meaningful drift
physical_basis: HVAC systems consume energy whenever conditioning persists beyond the real occupied or service-relevant boundary.
operational_basis: Schedules, overrides and weak controls governance can keep HVAC active outside useful windows.
financial_mechanism: Runtime drift can inflate consumption and sometimes demand, while also misleading analysts toward equipment-first narratives.
typical_false_assumption: If HVAC energy is high, equipment inefficiency must be the primary issue.
hypothesis: Schedule drift or after-hours HVAC runtime may be creating avoidable load before deeper retrofit logic is justified.
rival_hypotheses: runtime is already aligned to real duty
minimum_evidence_to_confirm: runtime materially exceeds occupied or service-relevant windows
controls evidence supports drift or weak scheduling
falsification_conditions: runtime aligns to occupied or service-relevant windows
after-hours conditioning is justified by real duty
allowed_claim_language: HVAC schedule drift is a plausible hypothesis requiring runtime and schedule validation.
prohibited_claim_language: This asset has HVAC schedule waste.
financial_exposure_if_true: controls-first action may outrank equipment CAPEX
consumption and demand can be misframed as equipment inefficiency
financial_exposure_if_false: attention should shift to competing HVAC or boundary drivers
stop_conditions: runtime and schedule alignment are bounded enough to rank the hypothesis
escalation_conditions: operator or facilities confirmation required if public evidence remains insufficient
claim_permissions_impact: block equipment-first retrofit framing without schedule evidence
example_outputs: Before buying equipment, determine whether the building is simply conditioning beyond the real duty window.
tests: building and warehouse cases with unresolved schedules should admit this as a bounded hypothesis
pattern must remain non-diagnostic at L2
